security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code examples for normal FastAPI configuration, tests, and authentication. I found two semantic security issues in the template guidance: missing object-level authorization on user reads and insecure credentialed wildcard CORS.

remediation.issue: The user read endpoint returns records by user_id without a matching ownership or role check.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit current_user.id comparison or admin role authorization before returning another user's record.

remediation.issue: The application example uses wildcard CORS origins while allowing credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Replace wildcard origins with an explicit allowlist from configuration, especially when credentials are enabled.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Object-Level Authorization on User Read
semantic_findings.description: The read_user endpoint fetches any user by user_id after authentication. It does not compare the record with current_user.id or an admin role.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The update and delete endpoints perform id checks, but read_user returns the fetched user without comparable authorization. No admin role check is shown.

semantic_findings.title: Permissive CORS Allows Credentialed Cross-Origin Access
semantic_findings.description: The template sets allow_origins to wildcard while allowing credentials. This can allow untrusted origins to make credentialed browser requests if copied into production.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The CORS settings are in the main application example, and no environment-specific restriction is shown. Users may adapt it, but the default guidance is unsafe.

content.value_statement: FastAPI projects need consistent structure, async database patterns, auth, testing, and error handling. This skill provides reusable templates and implementation guidance for production backend APIs.
actual_capabilities: Defines a layered FastAPI project layout with API, core, models, schemas, services, repositories, and tests.
Shows async database setup with SQLAlchemy sessions and dependency injection.
Provides repository and service layer examples for user workflows.
Includes JWT authentication and password hashing examples.
Outlines async test fixtures and endpoint tests with httpx.
limitations: It provides templates and guidance, not a complete generated application.
Example security settings need review before production use.
It focuses on FastAPI backends, not frontend or infrastructure automation.
Database and auth code may need updates for project-specific policies.

use_cases.title: Start a New API
use_cases.description: Create a structured FastAPI backend with async patterns and testing from the first iteration.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Templates
use_cases.description: Align service structure, repositories, configuration, and tests across several Python API projects.

use_cases.title: Review an Existing FastAPI App
use_cases.description: Compare an existing backend against layered architecture, dependency injection, auth, and testing patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the fastapi-templates skill to design a small FastAPI service for notes. Include folders, core modules, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Add Auth and Data Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to add JWT authentication, async SQLAlchemy sessions, repositories, and service logic to my FastAPI project.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing API
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this FastAPI codebase with the skill. Recommend changes for async database access, dependency injection, services, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Blueprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to plan a multi-module FastAPI backend. Include auth, database boundaries, testing strategy, and deployment checks.

output_examples.input: Create a new async API for user accounts.
output: A project layout with app, api, core, models, schemas, services, repositories, and tests.
Guidance for database settings, JWT authentication, and dependency injection.
A testing plan with async fixtures and endpoint coverage.
Findings on route boundaries, service placement, repository usage, and schema design.
Recommendations for async session handling, error handling, and test coverage.
Security notes for CORS, auth checks, secrets, and environment configuration.

best_practices: Review generated CORS, authentication, and database settings before production deployment.
Adapt repository and service layers to the domain model before adding endpoints.
Pair templates with tests that cover routes, services, database sessions, and auth failures.
anti_patterns: Do not use wildcard CORS settings with credentials in production.
Do not keep business logic inside route handlers.
Do not copy example secrets, database URLs, or test passwords into live environments.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands or install packages?
faq.answer: No. The files provide guidance and examples. A user or agent must choose any commands.

faq.question: Can it create complete FastAPI applications?
faq.answer: It can guide structure and code patterns. It does not ship a full runnable project by itself.

faq.question: Does it support async SQLAlchemy?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes async engine, session, repository, and test fixture patterns.

faq.question: Is the sample authentication production ready?
faq.answer: No. Treat it as a starting point. Review token, password, secret, and authorization rules.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Which projects fit this skill?
faq.answer: New Python API services, backend refactors, and teams standardizing FastAPI templates fit best.
